legal_basis: Council Bill 2026-147, enacted 2026-06-29 as Ordinance No. 28306 -- although, per a since-filed lawsuit, the ordinance was filed by the City Clerk using resolution-style 'be it resolved' language rather than 'be it ordained,' which the plaintiff argues is itself a charter defect. It imposes a 120-day administrative delay on data center applications/approvals set to expire 2026-11-17.
trigger: Pause on development, building, site-plan, variance, stormwater, conditional-use, occupancy, public-utility, and large-load electric applications for data centers while the City Manager studies recommendations
current_status: The October 23 city document schedules a November 16 vote on a proposed extension through February 24, 2027. No approved extension is established. Local reporting describes denial of the plaintiff’s temporary restraining order on October 23; denial is not a final judgment on validity or an exhaustive later-docket review. affected_projects: Exempts projects whose Southwest Power Pool study process had already begun with required fees submitted, and permits council-approved exceptions

date_enacted: 2026-03, East Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors vote to initiate a municipal curative amendment (Chester County); exact day not confirmed in sources reviewed
duration: 180 days from the March 2026 vote to draft and adopt a data-center zoning ordinance ('Data Center Ordinance'); a public hearing to consider its adoption was set for Sept. 24, 2026.
legal_basis: East Whiteland Township municipal curative amendment under the PA Municipalities Planning Code, developed with a resident working group beginning May 2026; a Sept. 24, 2026 public hearing was set to consider adoption of the resulting ordinance
trigger: Regulatory gap combined with a specific, highly contested project: developer Green Fig's proposal (later expanded to 1.7 million sq ft) for a data center on Swedesford Road, which drew sustained community opposition; the township already had an earlier, separately approved 2024 data-center plan on the same site.
current_status: Nearing resolution as of 2026-09-23. The 180-day curative-amendment clock started in March 2026 (per The Center Square); Green Fig withdrew its expanded 1.7-million-sq-ft application in May 2026 amid sustained opposition and signaled intent to instead pursue its earlier, previously approved 2024 plan. A resident working group helped draft the resulting 'Data Center Ordinance,' for which the Board of Supervisors set a Sept. 24, 2026 public hearing to consider adoption (one day after this research pass); the pending Sentinel/Green Fig application is not on that hearing's agenda.
affected_projects: Green Fig/Sentinel data center proposal on Swedesford Road; the expanded 1.7-million-sq-ft version was withdrawn in May 2026, with the developer expected to instead pursue its earlier-approved 2024 plan (details of that plan not confirmed in this pass).
outcome: East Whiteland Township Board of Supervisors initiated a municipal curative amendment in March 2026 to add data-center zoning standards; a resident working group helped draft the resulting ordinance, which was scheduled for a Sept. 24, 2026 adoption hearing.
